historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is negative (-2.8% 5yr) because buybacks and dividends ($1.5bn/yr) exceed net income; book value is not a growth proxy for this company. EPS 3yr CAGR (34%) is inflated by the depressed FY2022 COVID-lockdown base. Revenue 5yr CAGR used instead.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - interest income): FY2020 616, FY2022 608, FY2025 706. Owner-FCF 3yr CAGR (5.1%) is ABOVE reported (4.6%) because interest income fell from $169m (FY2023) to $92m as the cash pile was returned, not because SBC is small (SBC is ~0.4% of revenue, a non-issue). FCF growth lags revenue growth: margins compressed from the FY2021 peak and capex stepped up for the store rollout.

scenario_narratives.base: Yum China executes the RGM 3.0 plan roughly to guidance: ~1,900 net openings a year with 40-50% franchised, KFC same-store sales low single digit as transaction growth (+5%) is offset by falling average ticket in a deflationary China consumer, and the Pizza Hut brand buyout lifts group EBITDA margin ~0.6pp by removing the license fee. Delivery mix keeps rising toward ~55% and rider costs absorb most efficiency gains, so margins improve only modestly to 16.5% ex-SBC. Capital intensity eases with small-format stores; ~100% of FCF is returned from 2027.
scenario_narratives.bull: The 30,000-store/4,500-city target is reached on schedule with new-unit returns holding in lower-tier cities, KCOFFEE (5,000+) and Lavazza (1,000) scale into a real third leg, the 2026 regulatory de-escalation of delivery subsidies holds so rider/commission costs stabilise, and Pizza Hut margins converge toward KFC's after the buyout. Franchise mix and smaller formats cut capex per store, pushing ex-SBC EBITDA margin to 17.5% and revenue growth to 8-10% for five years.
scenario_narratives.bear: China consumer deflation persists: average ticket keeps falling (KFC -3% in Q2-2026), value-price wars with McDonald's, domestic burger chains and Luckin/Cotti re-ignite, and aggressive unit growth cannibalises existing stores in lower-tier cities. Delivery's rising share erodes restaurant margin, the Pizza Hut fee saving is competed away, and RMB weakness depresses USD revenue. Growth slows to 3-4% after FY2026 and ex-SBC margin drifts to 14.2%; PCAOB/HFCAA and US-China tensions are tail risks on the multiple, captured here only through the flows and the weight.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF valuation of China's largest restaurant operator on attributable, SBC-expensed, interest-stripped flows in USD at a USD-built 9.5% WACC, converted to HKD for the 9987.HK quote. The thesis is unit growth plus a modest margin lift from the Pizza Hut brand buyout and franchising, against a structurally soft China consumer.
key_risks_to_valuation: Average-ticket deflation and renewed price wars compress restaurant margins below the 16% band
Delivery mix (~54% of company sales) raises rider/commission costs faster than efficiency gains
RMB/USD translation: a 10% RMB depreciation cuts operating profit ~$75m per half-year (H1-2026 interim disclosure)
Master-license dependency on Yum! Brands for KFC and Taco Bell; Taco Bell development dispute unresolved
PCAOB inspection / HFCAA and US-China geopolitical tension affect the multiple and capital repatriation
Bridge-loan refinancing terms for the $1.2bn Pizza Hut acquisition are not yet set

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (9987.HK) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 310.6-451.2 HKD. USD/HKD from Yahoo HKD=X; YUMC NYSE quote used for parity.
data_sources.financials: Yum China FY2020-FY2025 annual reports and H1-2024/2025/2026 interim reports (HKEX), via 9987.HK_Metrics.csv and Extracted/ text; H1-2026 balance sheet and Note 15 (Pizza Hut acquisition and bridge loan).
data_sources.qualitative: 9987.HK_Analysis.json (2026-10-24): FY2026 guidance, Pizza Hut brand buyout, capital return plan, bull/bear cases.

inputs.share_count_basis: 345m common shares outstanding at 30-Jun-2026 (H1-2026 interim) plus ~1m dilutive SARs/RSUs (H1-2026 diluted weighted average 351m vs basic 350m). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, buybacks ($1.1bn planned 2026) are the cash mechanism that keeps the count flat and are value-neutral here. Shares are fungible 1:1 between NYSE (YUMC) and HKEX (9987.HK).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash-flow statement share-based compensation add-back ($42m); no separate combined figure published. Note Yum China's Adjusted EBITDA does NOT add back SBC, so the EBITDA margin path below is built ex-SBC ((Adj EBITDA + SBC)/revenue) and SBC is then charged once via sbc_pct_path.
inputs.fx_note: Flows and statements in USD (10-K / HKEX interim). Price is the HKEX secondary listing 9987.HK in HKD. USD->HKD 7.8413 from Yahoo HKD=X chart API, 2026-10-23 close (inside the 7.75-7.85 peg band). Parity check: NYSE YUMC USD 44.54 x 7.8413 = HKD 349.3 vs HKEX 354.2 (1.4% gap; HKEX closed ~12h before NYSE on 2026-10-23, fungible 1:1 shares). Per-share values computed in USD then converted; unsuffixed values are HKD.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD-built rate: US 10y ~4.3% + beta ~0.85 x 5.0% ERP + ~1.0pp China country-risk premium = ~9.5% cost of equity; company is net cash so WACC ~ CoE. Same WACC in all three scenarios: China consumer and geopolitical risk is priced in the bear flows and its 25% weight, not stacked as a per-scenario premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases: rent sits inside restaurant operating costs, so Adj EBITDA is already after the full lease charge (treatment B by construction). Lease liabilities ($2.3bn) are EXCLUDED from net debt; lease_cost_pct_path 0 to avoid a second charge. D&A is PP&E depreciation only (no ROU depreciation under ASC 842 operating leases).
inputs.nci_treatment: Attributable-only flows: NCI (Hangzhou/Suzhou KFC partner JVs, ~7% of consolidated net income: H1-2026 $42m of $595m) folded into the cash-tax/leakage driver (27% ETR + PRC dividend withholding + ~7% NCI share = 33%). No NCI deduction in the bridge (book NCI $704m), so NCI is charged once. Calibration: FY2025 Operating Profit 1,290 x (1-0.335) = 858 vs attributable NI 929 less ~72 after-tax interest income = ~857.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company, US-domiciled filer reporting USD, quoted HKD on HKEX) per dcf-methods routing, with the adaptations for dual currency, leases and NCI. First valuation of this ticker (no memory entry). Owner FCF FY2025 = reported FCF 840 (OCF 1,466 - capex 626) - SBC 42 - interest income 92 = 706. Interest income stripped because liquid holdings ($2.05bn) exceed 1x the FCF base; the matching cash is in the bridge. NET DEBT is pro-forma for the Pizza Hut mainland brand acquisition closed Aug-2026 ($1.2bn cash, funded by a ~$1.2bn offshore bridge loan): cash = cash 485 + short-term investments 901 + long-term bank deposits/notes 688 - 21 restricted = 2,053; debt = short-term borrowings 66 + bridge 1,200 = 1,266; net cash 787. H2-2026 buybacks and dividends after 30-Jun reduce both cash and shares and are not separately rolled forward (approximately value-neutral). Pizza Hut license fee (~3% of Pizza Hut system sales, ~$70m/yr) removal is in the margin path from FY2026 (4 months) and FY2027 (full). Buybacks are funded: $1,144m FY2025, $530m H1-2026, ~100% of FCF after NCI dividends from 2027.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026: H1 USD revenue +11% (+6% ex-FX), guidance mid-high single-digit system sales growth and >1,900 net new stores; full-year USD ~+9% with the FX tailwind fading in H2. Then ~7% (store growth ~8-9%/yr toward 30,000 by 2030, low single-digit SSS, partly offset by rising franchise mix which books royalties not sales) decelerating to 3.5%.
base.margin_rationale: Ex-SBC Adj EBITDA margin FY2025 15.1% (1,738+42)/11,797. FY2026 +0.2pp for 4 months of Pizza Hut license-fee removal, FY2027 full ~0.6pp; then +0.6pp from franchise mix and digital/labour efficiency to 16.5%, still below the FY2021 ~19.7% peak. Restaurant margin held ~16% as rider costs offset efficiency.
base.capex_rationale: FY2026 guidance $600-700m (~5.1% of revenue), trending down as smaller-format stores and franchise mix lower per-unit capex; terminal 4.2% vs D&A 3.6% supports 3% growth.
base.wc_rationale: Restaurant operator with negative working capital (payables and stored-value card liabilities exceed receivables/inventory): small positive capture on revenue growth.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 16x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: single-country exposure to a deflationary China consumer, a single-licensor dependency (Yum! Brands master license, Taco Bell milestone breach under renegotiation) and US-China/PCAOB tail risk. Base 50%: guidance has been reaffirmed through Q2-2026 with 14 straight quarters of transaction growth. Bull trimmed to 25% because it needs unit returns, delivery economics and new-brand scaling to all go right simultaneously.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
